t: Minimum Number of Steps to Make Two Strings Anagram II
o: We may append any characters to either s or t and want the minimum number of appends until the two are anagrams. For s = leetcode and t = coats we append "as" to s (2 steps) and "leede" to t (5 steps) for a total of 7; night and thing are already anagrams, so the answer is 0. Because order never matters, each string is fully summarized by its letter multiset: every surplus occurrence of a letter in one string must eventually be matched by an appended occurrence in the other. With lengths up to 2 * 10^5 but only 26 distinct letters, one frequency pass over each string plus a 26-slot comparison is all that is needed.
k: Anagram equality ignores order — only the multiset of letters matters.
For each letter, |count_s(c) - count_t(c)| appends are unavoidable and sufficient, since we may pad either string.
Equivalently the answer is |s| + |t| - 2 * overlap, where overlap sums min(count_s(c), count_t(c)) over letters.

a.i: Tally both strings into two length-26 arrays. After padding, both strings must agree exactly on every letter count, and each unit of disagreement between cs[c] and ct[c] costs exactly one append on the smaller side. Summing absolute differences over 26 letters therefore gives the exact minimum.
s: Build frequency arrays cs and ct of size 26.
Scan s once incrementing cs, then scan t once incrementing ct.
Sum abs(cs[c] - ct[c]) over all 26 letters.
a.t: O(|s| + |t| + 26) — one linear pass per string plus a constant-size comparison.

a.i: Think about which characters survive untouched: for each letter, min(cs[c], ct[c]) occurrences already match across the strings. Everything else must be appended to whichever string is short on that letter. So the answer is |s| + |t| minus twice the overlap total — each matched character spares one append in each string. A single counter with greedy matching while scanning t computes the overlap without a second array.
s: Count the letters of s into cnt.
Scan t, decrementing cnt and counting keep whenever the letter is still available.
a.t: O(|s| + |t| + 26) — same linear scans as Approach 1.

w: Either framing is a clean O(n) interview answer; the difference formula is worth stating aloud because it shows you understand why padding is optimal — no append can ever help two letters at once. The classic trap is confusing this with LeetCode 1347, where appends were allowed only into t and the answer was sum of max(cs - ct, 0); here padding is symmetric, hence the absolute values. Edge case: identical multisets return 0 immediately. Follow-ups include streaming versions (maintain counts under character insertions and report steps online) or alphabets beyond lowercase, where hash maps replace the fixed arrays.
